description: Bai Fen (literally 'Hundred Points') is a foundational Chinese trick-taking game that serves as the progenitor to more complex multi-deck games like Tractor (Sheng Ji). Played with a single 54-card deck, it is a game of partnership survival where the Attacking team tries to capture specific point cards (5s, 10s, and Kings) while the Defending team protects their lead. It features a trump system where a trump rank is rotated and combined with jokers to create a powerful hierarchy.

content.text: Bai Fen (literally 'Hundred Points') is a foundational Chinese trick-taking game that serves as the progenitor to more complex multi-deck games like Tractor (Sheng Ji). Played with a single 54-card deck, it is a game of partnership survival where the Attacking team tries to capture specific point cards (5s, 10s, and Kings) while the Defending team protects their lead. It features a trump system where a trump rank is rotated and combined with jokers to create a powerful hierarchy.

Originating in Northern China as a simplified version of the older 'Zheng Fen' (Compete for Points) games. It standardized the '100 Point' economy of a single deck, making it accessible to a wider audience before the 1980s explosion of multi-deck 'Tractor' variants.
One standard 52-card deck plus both Jokers (Red and Black).
The deck is shuffled and players draw one card at a time until the deck is exhausted. The dealer role rotates clockwise.

items.text: Da Bai Fen (Great 100): Uses a 'Leveling' system where winning a hand allows you to promote your Trump Rank (e.g., from 2 to 3).
